title: Finitely many maximal ideals over a nonzero element
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For every nonzero $x \in R$, the set $\{\mathfrak m \subset R : \mathfrak m\text{ is maximal and }x \in \mathfrak m\}$ is finite.

proof.text: Let I=xR. By [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal], the finite set I.minimalPrimes consists of the prime ideals minimal among those containing xR.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PF, proof lines 29275-29279 (finiteness of primes over x)

proof.text: If m is maximal and x belongs to m, [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] applied to I=xR gives p in I.minimalPrimes with p subseteq m. Since R is a domain and x is nonzero, p is nonzero. The chain (0) subsetneq p subseteq m cannot have a strict second inclusion when dim R=1, by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; hence p=m. Thus every maximal ideal containing x lies in the finite set I.minimalPrimes.
